Metro RDT}} The '''Ahmedabad Metro''' is a [[rapid transit]] system for the cities of [[Ahmedabad]], [[Gandhinagar]], and [[GIFT City]] in the state of [[Gujarat]] in [[India]]. Currently the network is {{cvt|67.56|km|3}} long and has [[List of Ahmedabad Metro stations|54]] operational stations.{{Cite web |title=Ahmedabad Metro - Information, Route Maps, Fares, Tenders & Updates |url=https://themetrorailguy.com/ahmedabad-metro-information-map-updates/ |access-date=2024-09-22 |website=The Metro Rail Guy |language=en-US}} The [[Gujarat Metro Rail Corporation Limited]] was established in February 2010 and the {{cvt|40.03|km|3}} Phase 1 of the project was approved in October 2013 with two corridors, North–South and East–West. Construction started on 14 March 2015. A {{Cvt|6.5|km|3}} section of the East–West corridor was inaugurated on 4 March 2019. The rest of Phase 1 was inaugurated on 30 September 2022, except the Thaltej Gam end and three stations.{{Cite web |date=2024-06-06 |title=Ahmedabad Metro Route Map, Station List, Progress and Latest Updates - Infra Info Hub |url=https://infrainfohub.com/ahmedabad-metro/ |access-date=2024-07-15 |language=en-US}} Phase 1 was completed in December 2024, except Sabarmati Railway Station metro station. Phase 2 was approved in February 2019 and construction started in January 2021. The Violet Line and part of the Yellow line opened in September 2024. The rest of the Yellow Line opened gradually, concluding with the completion of Phase 2 in January 2026. ==Background== [[File:The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi inaugurating the Ahmedabad Metro in Ahmedabad, Gujarat on September 30, 2022.jpg|thumb|left|Prime Minister [[Narendra Modi]] inaugurating the metro on 30 September 2022.]] In 2003, Gujarat Infrastructure Development Board carried out a study for urban transport between Gandhinagar and Ahmedabad. It also carried out the detailed project report through [[Delhi Metro Rail Corporation]] and [[RITES Limited|RITES]] and submitted it in June 2005 and received Central Government's approval in the same year.{{Cite news|url=http://www.dnaindia.com/india/report_from-2015-ride-metro-from-ahmedabad-to-gandhinagar_1746745|title=From 2015, ride Metro from Ahmedabad to Gandhinagar|date=2012-09-29|work=dna|access-date=2018-10-21|language=en-US}}{{cite news|url=http://www.business-standard.com/india/storypage.php?autono=340107 |title=Ahmedabad metro rail project put on fast track |work=Business Standard|access-date=2010-07-27}} Following the estimated cost of {{INRconvert|4295|c}} and the study of the viability of the project, it was abandoned in 2005 to give priority to the [[Ahmedabad BRTS]] and [[Ahmedabad Suburban Railway|suburban railway]] projects. In 2008, considering the future developments in and around Ahmedabad and Gandhinagar, the project was revived and new corridors designed to make the project viable.{{Cite web |date=October 24, 2009 |first=Paul |last=John |title=Metro rail project holds huge potential for realty biz: DMRC |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/ahmedabad/metro-rail-project-holds-huge-potential-for-realty-biz-dmrc/articleshow/5154617.cms |access-date=2022-09-30 |website=The Times of India |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=June 11, 2009 |first=Paul |last=John |title=Ahmedabad-Gandhinagar Metro project: Is there light at the end of Metro tunnel? |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/ahmedabad/ahmedabad-gandhinagar-metro-project-is-there-light-at-the-end-of-metro-tunnel/articleshow/4641855.cms |access-date=2022-09-30 |website=The Times of India |language=en}} The special purpose vehicle company, Metro Link Express for Gandhinagar and Ahmedabad Company Ltd, later renamed [[Gujarat Metro Rail Corporation Limited]] (GMRC) in 2018, was established by [[Government of Gujarat]] on 4 February 2010 with {{INRconvert|202|c}}. Later in 2014, it was decided that the Central Government will own 50% of the company.{{cite web|url=http://www.dnaindia.com/india/report_new-firm-to-speed-up-metro-in-ahmedabad_1252343 |title=New firm to speed up Metro in Ahmedabad |work=Daily News and Analysis |date=2009-05-02 |access-date=2010-07-27}}{{cite news|title=Ahemedabad Metro project gets green signal|website=The Times of India|date=17 October 2014|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/ahmedabad/Ahemedabad-Metro-project-gets-green-signal/articleshow/44870418.cms|access-date=2014-10-18}} == Construction Phases == === Phase 1 === The {{cvt|40.03|km|3}} Phase 1 of the project was approved in October 2013 with two corridors, North–South and East–West. On 19 October 2014, [[Union Cabinet of India]] approved {{INRconvert|10773|c}} for Phase 1. The Central Government approved the use of unused [[Western Railways]] land along the Botad-Sabarmati meter gauge line in November 2014.{{cite web | author=India | title=Modi government clears Railway land for Ahmedabad metro project | website=The Indian Express | date=5 November 2014 | url=http://indianexpress.com/article/cities/ahmedabad/modi-government-clears-railway-land-for-ahmedabad-metro-project/ | access-date=2015-02-25}} The original plan of Metro along Ashram Road was tweaked and the track was moved westward. The new plan added the cost of {{INRconvert|600|c}} and two more stations. The new plan helped by causing fewer problems in land acquisition and less congestion on Ashram Road. In 2015 budget of Gujarat, {{INRconvert|611|c}} was further allocated for the metro. The ground breaking ceremony was held on 14 March 2015 for the construction of the {{Cvt|6.5|km|3}} Vastral–Apparel Park stretch of the East–West corridor (Blue Line) in the presence of the then Gujarat Chief Minister, [[Anandiben Patel]]. The ground-breaking ceremony for the North–South Corridor (Red Line) was held on 17 January 2016 in the presence of the then Gujarat CM Anandiben Patel. The work started in March 2016.{{cite web|url=http://indianexpress.com/article/cities/ahmedabad/mumbai-based-firm-wins-bid-for-ahmedabad-metro-construction/|title=Mumbai-based firm wins bid for Over 7.1 lakh people had travelled by metro till June 2022 but the monthly ridership had never exceeded 38,137 which is the highest ridership registered in March 2019 due to short length of the opened corridor then. The most riders were identified as those taking joyrides. Following opening of the Phase-1 in September 2022, the ridership increased significantly. In FY 2025-26 (April 2025 to March 2026) more than 5,10,29,000 people travelled via metro with average daily ridership of 1,53,871 in January 2026.{{Cite web |date=2026-04-10 |title=Ahmedabad Metro Rail Passenger journey|url=https://www.gujaratmetrorail.com/ahmedabad/ |access-date=2026-04-10 |website=GMRC|language=en-US}} {{Bar chart | title = Yearly ridership | label_type = Year | data_type = Ridership | bar_width = 30 | width_units = em | data_max = 30000000 | label1 = March 2019 | data1 = 38,137 | label2 = 2019–20 | data2 = 2,84,934 | label3 = 2020–21 | data3 = 46,570 | label4 = 2021–22 | data4 = 2,41,694 | label5 = October 2022–23 | data5 = 734,3,63 | label6 = 2023–24 | data6 = 29346000 | label7 = 2024–25 | data7 = 40068000 | label8 = 2025–26 | data8 = 51029000 }} ==Controversy== [[File:Ahmedabad Metro Red Line 03.jpg|thumb|left|Ahmedabad Metro Red Line Interior]] Near Thaltej Gam on western side, 300-odd shop owners opposed the land acquisition while the officials said that there is need of huge land for depot and parking for the project.{{cite web | title=Tenders issued for Metro construction - TOI Mobile | website=The Times of India Mobile Site | date=30 January 2015 | url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/ahmedabad/Tenders-issued-for-Metro-construction/articleshow/46060476.cms | access-date=2015-02-25}} The land acquisition is also opposed by the residents and shop owners of Jivraj Park in Vejalpur area. They had filed a case in [[Gujarat High Court]].{{cite web | title=Ahmedabad metro project: MEGA offers relocation option to residents| website=ETRealty.com | date=23 March 2016 | url=http://realty.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/residential/ahmedabad-metro-project-mega-offers-relocation-option-to-residents/51526241 | access-date=8 April 2016}}{{cite web | title=Metro rail project: Residents of Vejalpur junk relocation offer | website=The Indian Express | date=30 March 2016 | url=http://indianexpress.com/article/cities/ahmedabad/metro-rail-project-residents-of-vejalpur-junk-relocation-offer/ | access-date=8 April 2016}} They settled the case in September 2017.{{Cite news|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/ahmedabad/metro-project-clears-hurdle-in-land-acquisition/articleshow/60757061.cms|title=Metro project clears hurdle in land acquisition|date=2017-09-03|work=The Times of India|access-date=2017-09-27}} Former IAS officer and executive chairman of project [[Sanjay Gupta (businessman)|Sanjay Gupta]] and seven of his subordinate officers were accused while two of them were arrested in May 2015 for alleged committed fraud of {{INRconvert|113|c}} in procurement and use of ground filling materials for the project in 2012.
